findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the triple sink had a steady leak at the faucet. PIC is aware of the issue and plans to get it repaired as soon as the plumber is available. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an old vent in the kitchen that was “closed” with a rag, which is an absorbent material that is not being cleaned regularly. PIC was notified and made plans to replace the seal. Options include sealing it off fully with metal or a similar covering, or a screen that can be cleaned and prevent pests and maintain airflow. Ensure that all surfaces are constructed to smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas that need to be cleaned with more frequency:
(A) the microwave,
(B) the walls behind the stove and fryer.
PIC was notified and made plans to clean these areas. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer spray bottle was testing too strong during the inspection (over 200ppm (Cl); the test strip was bleaching out). The PIC dumped the spray bottle and re-made it which tested at 150 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizer bottles are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the bar ice scoop was stored with the handle touching the ice. The PIC was educated and the handle was moved above the ice. Ensure that handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above the top of food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that no one at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that all CFPM’s obtain basic training in allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Single service forks are stored with tines and handles mixed. Face single service utensils and store them properly protected. 

 (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.
